key_insight: A small subset of PSO-X modules and their pairwise interactions explain most of the variation in optimization performance, so understanding both main effects and interactions lets you dramatically reduce configuration complexity.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of selecting and configuring dozens of interacting modules in the PSO-X modular particle swarm optimization framework by quantifying which modules and interactions truly matter for performance.
method: Large-scale, controlled experiments over benchmark continuous optimization problems sampling configurations across PSO-X modules.
Variance-decomposition and interaction analysis (e.g., ANOVA/Sobol-style sensitivity) to measure main effects and pairwise interactions of modules.
Ranking and visualization of module importance to identify the minimal set of modules/interactions that drive performance.
impact: Enables practitioners to focus tuning and AutoML search on the most influential modules and interactions, reducing configuration cost and improving robustness of PSO-based optimizers.
visual_elements: Bar chart of module importance (main effects) ranked by explained performance variance
Heatmap of pairwise interaction strengths between modules
Schematic of the experimental/factorial sampling pipeline (modules → configurations → benchmarks → analysis)
Performance distributions (boxplots) comparing full configurations vs. reduced/high-impact-subset configurations
paper_title: Quantifying the Impact of Modules and Their Interactions in the PSO-X Framework
paper_authors: Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski
